title: CRLR/95/2017 of Pankaj Sharma Vs Nilam

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Delay Condonation Application No. 603 of 2017
In
Criminal Revision No. 95 of 2017
Pankaj Sharma Ö..Revisionist
Versus
Smt. Nilam Ö.Respondent
Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, Advocate for the revisionist.
There is no representation for the respondent.
Dated: 26.07.2017
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.
 Heard.
2. Delay Condonation Application, being
unopposed by the respondent, is allowed. Delay in
filing the criminal revision is condoned.
3. This criminal revision has been preferred by
the revisionist against the judgment and order dated
11.11.2016 passed by the Additional Principal Judge,
Family Court, Rishikesh, District Dehradun in Case
No. 63 of 2014 ìSmt. Nilam v. Pankaj Sharmaî under
Section 125 of Cr.P.C., whereby the Additional
Principal Judge, Family Court has partly allowed the
application of respondent under Section 125 Cr.P.C.
and the revisionist is directed to pay the maintenance
to the respondent @ ` 5000/- per month.
4. The matter was placed before the Mediation
Centre of this Court. In the mediation proceeding, the
parties have arrived at following compromise:
ì1. That during the course of mediation
the parties have decided to live separately
and they will get the mutual divorce from
the competent Court within a period of six
month from today and there will be no
objection for the either side.

2
2. The husband Revisionist will pay sum
of ` 4,00,000/- (Rupees four lakh only) as
a full and final settlement towards the
permanent alimony of divorce and arrear
of maintenance as per the order passed by
the Judge, Family Court. She will not
claim or entitled to get any further amount
from her husband Mr. Pankaj Sharma.
3. The husband-revisionist will pay
` 4,00,000/- (Rupees four lakh only) to the
respondent-wife on or before 15.10.2017,
by Bank Draft, thereafter only the divorce
will effect between the parties and this
revision will be decided in the above terms.
4. That the parties hereto confirm and
declare that they have voluntarily and out
of their own free will arrived at this
settlement/ agreement in the presence of
the respective counsel.
5. That the settlement has been read
over and explained to the parties in their
own language. Signature of parties are also
identified by their advocates.
6. That both the parties are bound by
the terms and conditions of this settlement
agreement and the wife will not filed any
case against husband and all the cases
pending in any other Court shall be
withdrawn by the wife and the husband
also will not file any case against the wife.
7. The contents of the settlement have
been explained to the parties in vernacular
and they have understood the same and
have affirmed the same to be correct.î
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist
submitted that the settlement arrived at by the parties
be recorded.
6. The settlement report of the Mediator in the
form of settlement is already on the record.

3
7. Learned counsel for the revisionist then
submitted that the revision be dismissed as not
pressed.
8. In view of above stated facts, the prayer is
allowed and revision is dismissed as not pressed.
9. All the pending applications also stand
disposed of.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
26.07.2017
Navin
